title: FedGain: Toward Negative-Gain-Free Client Collaboration in Federated Learning
claim: Heterogeneity makes global training hurt data-rich clients; sifting effective capacity and clustering collaborators restores gains.
layout: 3 panels: large left problem panel, right top and bottom panels; lettered A-C
description: The figure has three boxed panels. Panel A on the left, 'Negative Gains Phenomenon', shows two scatter rings of points: blue IID data and orange/red non-IID data. A large green 'Local' circle sits between them, with green circular arrows showing local training. A dashed red line labeled 'Model Drift' runs down to a boxed 'Negative Gains' label with a red minus sign. Below that, a down arrow points to 'Global Training Performance'. Panel B, top right, 'Sift Effective Capacity', shows two clients c_i and c_j feeding a funnel that turns M_total into M_eff. Next to it is a loss-versus-M_total plot with a blue IID curve and a red non-IID curve. Panel C, bottom right, 'FL within each Cluster', shows clients (laptops, phones) grouped into solid ellipses around a gray cloud server. Dashed circles hold colored shapes for the data in each cluster.
caption: Negative Gains and Optimization of Client Collaboration.
abstract: Data heterogeneity is a fundamental challenge in Federated Learning (FL), where induced model drift often results in "negative gains" for global models on data-abundant clients, with performance falling below that of local training. To address this issue, we propose FedGain, a novel framework that optimizes collaborative client clustering to mitigate the negative gain. We are the first to develop a modified Scaling Law (SL) to quantify the reduction in data utility caused by heterogeneity and define Effective Federated Capacity to align clients with the highest potential collaboration gains. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our modified SL strictly adheres to the power-law learning discipline in non-IID scenarios. FedGain effectively suppresses negative gains to a negligible level across various FL algorithms and outperforms other Clustered FL methods.
